chapter_theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 20 of 21): after two long songs on lovemaking and on women's eyes, the chapter turns to short songs that ask not to be born again, for the experience of the feet, for the word beyond the quarrelling scriptures, and against singing for deceitful patrons; Murugan appears as Sambandar who impaled the Jains, and three akam songs give the lovesick girl's plight under Kama, the sea, the cuckoo and the moon.
structure_note: Four long songs (1277 to 1280), then short eight-line songs (1281 to 1291, with 1289 longer). 1285 and 1291 are two versions of one akam song (Kama's arrows, the blue sea, the cuckoo, 'embrace the deer'), and 1290 is a third on the moon and the south wind. 1282 and 1287 both end with Murugan as Sambandar.

1277.reading: The poet describes lovemaking in full motion, eyes battling, earrings, breasts, bangles and garlands swaying, honey dripping from the flowered hair, two becoming one body in maya, and vows that even then he will not forget Murugan's twelve arms, six faces, kadamba-garlanded chest and two feet. The praise calls him the child of grace of the dancing Kali, Bhairavi and trident-bearer who burned Tripura, Sivai of Kailasa, daughter of the mountain, and the guru who spoke into Siva's ear, whose garland rests on the Kuratti's breasts.
1277.nuance: Unusually the plea does not ask to escape the embrace: மாயை படுபோதும் ... மறவேனே, 'even when I fall into maya I will not forget', makes remembrance of the Lord hold within the act itself. அரன் ஒரு காதில் ஓது: Murugan teaching Siva in the ear, Om not named. The goddess is given a run of fierce names (காளி, பயிரவி, மோடி, சூலி) before the gentle ones.

1278.reading: The poet lists women's red spear-eyes that cut the lives of men and sages, their fragrant hair, smiles, musk-painted breasts, sweet lips, navel and waist, and asks whether Murugan will not lovingly think to grant, beyond that union, the cruel miry life and endless births, the great pure state of silent supreme bliss. The praise is a head-to-foot picture of Murugan: six faces, jewelled forehead ornament, twelve eyes of compassion and twelve earrings, lotus hands, sacred thread, waist-bells, anklets, peacock and vel, the beautiful Kumara, son of three-eyed Siva who melts with the mountain's daughter.
1278.nuance: The song sets two catalogues against each other: the woman's body part by part in the plea, and Murugan's form part by part in the praise, so that beauty is redirected rather than renounced. ஒரு மவுன பரமசுக சுத்தப் பெரும்பதம் names the goal as silence and bliss. புண்டாணகச் சுழிமடு is hard to divide.

1279.reading: The poet asks not to wander sharpening infatuation, caught in the torment of women whose voices are like the vina and whose eyes are poison and spear-points, nor to perish greedily piling up house and wealth, but that Murugan feed the scripture of knowledge into the nest where life dwells and show him the true state. The praise calls him the one who dwells in the land of the Veda, the gracious Vel who heard Nakkirar's composition set to song, who embraces the hunter girl of the high forest, and who set fire to the demons' land and freed the gods from prison.
1279.nuance: ஆவியுறை கூட்டில் ஞானமறை ஊட்டி: the body is the nest of the life, to be fed with knowledge rather than with women and wealth. கீரர் இயல் கேட்ட names Nakkirar, the poet of the Tirumurugatruppadai, as one whose poem Murugan received. The line on hunters of the knowledge path who sought a tank (கேணியுற வேட்ட ஞானநெறி வேட்டர்) is obscure, and ஆணியுள வீட்டை is unclear.

1280.reading: The poet, wandering infatuated in the danger of women whose tormenting eyes equal the sea, the sword, the halahala poison and Kama's arrows, asks to leave that tumult, have the distortion of the gunas run off and grow clear, and be given the greatness of joining the path of the unspeakable supreme form of knowledge. The praise names Rama who loosed the arrow that split Vali's chest and the seven sal trees, the blue-bodied Vishnu who blew the conch, Murugan as his nephew who uproots the base, and the lord who unites with the hunters' peacock-like girl.
1280.nuance: குணவிகாரம் ஓட: the disturbance of the qualities must run away before clarity (தெளிய) comes, and the goal is கூறொணா தற்பரம ஞானரூபம், the supreme knowledge-form that cannot be spoken. The conch episode (அமரேசன் ஒலிக்க வளை ஊதி மோகித்து விழ) is not clear to me, nor வெருப at the end of line 2.

1281.reading: The poet asks not to be born on this earth, not to mix with cheats, not to grow weary reciting the three Tamils, and to be given release. The praise calls Murugan the guru of true knowledge of the tattvas, the one whose form is sound, the eternal good life, and the light of the world who dances.
1281.nuance: முத்தமிழை ஓதித் தளராதே seems to set even the recitation of Tamil among the things that wear one out, perhaps poems recited for patrons as in 1284; the plain sense is uncertain. சத்த சொரூபா: Murugan as sound itself.

1282.reading: The poet asks that the chain of his binding deeds be removed and that he be given the state that, triumphant and in bliss, overflowing with love like the nectar of the milk ocean, desires that end. The praise says Murugan, having resolved it in mind, took a small form and danced the bharata to the beat, and as Sambandar filled the land with Tamil so that those who do penance to end their bonds had their want removed.
1282.nuance: சம்பந்தன் எனத் தமிழ் தேக்கிய: Murugan identified with the child-saint Sambandar, whose small form (சிறுவடிவு) and dancing are those of the boy. The second half of the plea (அந்தந்தனில் இச்சைகொள் ஆற்பதம்) is hard to construe.

1283.reading: The poet asks not to be born again oozing out of a womb, not to wander in heavy suffering, and that Murugan protect him so that the experience of his holy golden feet may flourish. The praise calls him the one who belongs to those free of attachment, the ornament of the beyond, holder of the cock banner, the light of the world.
1283.nuance: அநுபூதி, direct experience of the feet, is the goal, a word that recurs in 1293 and 1294. பரப்பற்றாருக்கு உரியோனே: he belongs to those who have cut their clinging. The glyph ஡ in line 1 stands for ஊ (கருப்பற்றூறி).

1284.reading: The poet asks not to be churned about, born from seed in the womb, and not to recite colourful Tamil poems that please deceitful scoundrels; he says Murugan regards him as one who praised him longing to be held. The praise names the Vel whose Sakti weapon pierced the mountain, the peacock delighting in seizing serpents, the one whose fame spreads in battle, and the lord who took the Kuratti's hand in the millet field.
1284.nuance: கபட்ட சட்டர்க்கு இதத்த சித்ரத் தமிழ்கள் உரையாதே: the refusal to spend Tamil on flattering false patrons, so that praise is kept for the Lord. The line வெளிப்படப் பற்றிடப்படுத்தத் தருக்கி மகிழ்வோனே is obscure and my reading of the plea's second half is tentative.

1285.reading: An akam plea in the voice of the girl's mother or friend: tormented by the arrows of cruel Kama, the roaring blue sea and the cuckoo of the grove, the deer-like girl has lost her composure, so let Murugan embrace her. The praise calls him dear to Siva who wears the serpent, the learned poet who knows the arts, Vela, harbour of his devotees' love, the six-faced lord.
1285.nuance: நிலைமை கெடு மானைத் தழுவாயே: the plea is not for release but for the god's embrace of the lovesick girl. The sea's roar and the cuckoo's call are the classical tormentors of separation. Nearly the same song stands at 1291.

1286.reading: The poet asks not to wander in the great net of women with Meru-like breasts, and whether Murugan cannot think to rule this dog so that he may rise each day. The praise names the one who taught knowledge so that souls may be saved, who bears twelve shoulders, who is dear to Siva who rides the bull, and the six-faced lord of the elephant-maiden.
1286.nuance: நாயேனை ஆள: the plea is to be taken as servant. மாதானை may be மாது ஆனை, Devayanai, or a great army; I take the first.

1287.reading: The poet asks to leave the vain devotion of the sects and, seeking the worship of Siva at the lotus feet, to be given grace through the true guru's scriptures and teaching. The praise names Murugan as the one who drank the milk of Uma's breast and spoke grace, made true penance his own, showed the farther shore of Tamil teaching, and impaled the Jains, that is, as Sambandar.
1287.nuance: சமய பத்தி வ்ருதா: devotion within the sects is vain, but Siva-worship (சிவார்ச்சனை) is not counted a sect. உமைமுலைத் தரு பால், சமணரைக் கழுவேற்றிய: the unmistakable details of Sambandar, given here to Murugan.

1288.reading: The poet asks whether he will gain the word of the heart that is not settled in the mass of quarrelling scriptures nor in the six-fold seat, and that is hard to gain even by the rare Vedas. The praise calls Murugan the one who fought the demons as the seven seas roared, and the close companion of poets who sing to gain wealth from his feet.
1288.nuance: சருவிய சாத்திரத் திரள்: the scriptures that quarrel, as in 1287's vain sects. சடுதிகழ் ஆஸ்பதம் may be the six systems, and அனிதய வார்த்தை, perhaps a word from the heart or beyond it, is obscure. பொருள் அடியால் பெறக் கவிபாடும் புலவர் can also mean poets who seek the meaning through the feet.

1289.reading: The poet asks whether he will escape the road to the deceit of women who rage and hiss, laugh and talk to bind him in infatuation, flaunt their breasts and half hide them in cloth, tend him until his mind is soothed, and then plunder his wealth. The praise recalls Murugan seeking a way to unite with the Kuratti guarding the millet field while bees sang, coaxing her unseen by her clansmen, and asks him for his feet as the one who fought until Sura died.
1289.nuance: தனத்தைச் சூறைகொள் மடவார்: the wealth taken is named, and சதி (deceit) closes the list. The praise sets Murugan's own secret courtship of Valli, hidden from her kin, against the women's false intimacy.

1290.reading: An akam plea: should the innocent girl suffer because of the moon that rises to harm her, the south wind that scatters fire, and Kama who dances with his flowers? The praise names the king who punished Brahma of the Veda, the chest the hunter's doll desires, the Vel that struck the mango in the sea, the lord of the speechless gods.
1290.nuance: The tormentors are the stock of the evening of separation: moon, south wind, Kama (அநங்கன்). ஓதச் சூதம் எறிந்த வேலா: Sura as the mango tree in the sea. ஊமைத் தேவர்கள் may be the gods struck dumb, perhaps for not knowing Om; I cannot place it.

1291.reading: A variant of 1285: by Kama's leaping arrows, the long blue sea and the cuckoo coming softly from the grove, the girl's body melts, and Murugan is asked to embrace her. The praise calls him the one clear in singing lucid Tamil, the valiant Kumaresa, whose anklets of knowledge Valli worships, Valli's bridegroom.
1291.nuance: Line for line the same frame as 1285 with different adjectives (துள்ளும், தொல்லை, மெள்ள, மெய்யுருகு), as if two drafts of one song survive. வள்ளல் தொழு may refer to Valli or to a generous devotee.

links.note: The same four lines of plea, Kama's arrows, the blue sea, the cuckoo of the grove and 'embrace the deer', with only the epithets changed; the two read as variants of one song.
Both songs end by naming Murugan as Sambandar: 1282 by name and by his child's dance, 1287 by the milk of Uma and the impaling of the Jains, and both credit him with filling the land with Tamil.
The Kural warns that the sweet words of women who want wealth, not love, bring harm; 1289 dramatizes those words (laughing talk, soothing care) and ends with the plunder of wealth.

1277 vows that even while two become one body in maya (மாயை படுபோதும்) the poet will not forget Murugan's arms, faces and feet (மறவேனே). Tirumanthiram 2857 says the Lord is himself the union and the sulking (புணரும் அவனே புலவி அவனே). The song keeps remembrance alive inside the embrace; the Tirumanthiram goes further and makes the embrace itself the Lord.

1278 asks, beyond women's embrace and endless births, for the pure great state of silent supreme bliss (ஒரு மவுன பரமசுக சுத்தப் பெரும்பதம்). Tirumanthiram 2844 names the true form as speechless bliss and silence (உரையற்ற ஆனந்த மோன சொரூபம்). Both join silence and bliss as one final state; the Tirumanthiram adds its analysis through the letters of Om.

1279 calls the body the nest where life dwells (ஆவியுறை கூட்டில்) and asks that it be fed the scripture of knowledge instead of women and wealth. Kural 338 likens the bond of body and life to a bird flying off and leaving its nest (குடம்பை) empty. The Kural uses the nest to show the bird will leave it; the song asks what the bird should be fed while it is still there.

1280 asks that the distortion of the gunas run off (குணவிகாரம் ஓட) so that he grows clear and joins the unspeakable supreme form of knowledge. Tirumanthiram 2296 maps sattva, rajas and tamas onto waking, dream and sleep, and says the gunaless state that ends them is stainless turiya (மாய்த்திடும் நிற்குணம் மாசில் துரியமே). The Tirumanthiram supplies the map of the state the song only names as clarity beyond the gunas.

1283 asks not to be born oozing from the womb again (கருப்பற்று ஊறிப் பிறவாதே) and for the experience of the holy golden feet. Tirumanthiram 1597 says that Nandi as guru placed his feet on the poet's head so that the path to the womb was drained away (கருவழி வாற்றிட). What the song asks, the Tirumanthiram reports as done: the feet close the womb-path.

1281 asks, among other things, not to grow weary reciting the three Tamils (முத்தமிழை ஓதித் தளராதே), which is hard to read alone. 1284 spells out the danger: not to recite colourful Tamil poems that please deceitful scoundrels (கபட்ட சட்டர்க்கு இதத்த சித்ரத் தமிழ்கள் உரையாதே). Read together, the weariness of 1281 is likely Tamil spent on patrons rather than on the Lord.

1287 asks to leave the vain devotion of the sects (சமய பத்தி வ்ருதா) and seek the worship of Siva at the lotus feet. Tirumanthiram 1534 declares the six sects nothing but waste (அவமல்லதில்லை அறுசமயங்கள்) and bids one cling to Nandi's feet and be saved. Both set the feet against the sects; neither counts Siva-worship itself as a sect.

1288 asks for a word of the heart that is not settled in the mass of quarrelling scriptures (சருவிய சாத்திரத் திரள்) nor in the six-fold seat, and is hard to gain even by the Vedas. Tirumanthiram 1533 says those who saw the six sects did not see him, and he is not the thing they hold (ஆறு சமயப் பொருளும் அவனலன்). Both place what is sought outside the systems; the Tirumanthiram adds a way, clarity upon clarity (தேறித் தெளிமின்).

1289 describes women who laugh and talk, tend a man until his mind is soothed, and then plunder his wealth (தனத்தைச் சூறைகொள் மடவார்). Naladiyar 377 has the worthless woman lick like a wild cow, take the wealth from his hands (அவர்கைப் பொருள்கொண்டு) and then balk like an ox. Both show the same sequence, tender care first and the seizure of wealth after.

source_issues: 1279: corrupt glyph in மிடறு஡ட்டு, read மிடறூட்டு (flagged by CORRUPT_CHARS).
1280: ஞான்ரு பத்தின் in line 8 should probably be ஞானரூபத்தின்.
1283: corrupt glyph in கருப்பற்று஡றி, read கருப்பற்றூறி (flagged by CORRUPT_CHARS).
1287: a stray space after the vowel உ splits words at line starts (உ மைமுலை, உ ரிய).
